grades.quote: Separating acquisition of inode pointers from locking helps avoid deadlock in some situations, for example during directory lookup. Multiple processes can hold a C pointer to an inode returned by iget, but only one process can lock the inode at a time.
grades.reason: Directly explains the separation: iget hands out inode pointers (references) that many processes can hold, while ilock gives exclusive access and loads content. It also gives the rationale, which is avoiding deadlock, for example during directory lookup. It does not name the ref count field explicitly.

grades.quote: Serializes operations on each inode and its content
grades.reason: The passage is only a table of xv6 locks. It says itable.lock protects allocation of in-memory inode entries and ip->lock serializes operations on an inode and its content. That hints at a split between allocation and reference management on one side and per-inode exclusive access on the other. It never mentions reference counts or explains why the two mechanisms are separate.
